reader_notes: Passage is fluent, idiomatic English journalism; the jars/shelf metaphor is carried consistently from the opening to the closing line without straining.
The two glossed terms (accession, regeneration) are also defined inline in the body, so the glossary is redundant but not confusing.
Q2 requires care: option B is the same claim as the correct one plus an unsupported 'without any limit' extension. That is a fair but demanding discrimination for a reader working at speed.

Q4 pits a true-but-generic statement (seeds must be regenerated before they lose germination) against the statement that actually explains the between-section difference (length of the wait). Both are supported facts; only one answers the 'why the difference' stem. Defensible, but this is the hardest item in the unit.
The writer is referred to as 'she' in Q5 while the byline is 'Petra Lindholm' - consistent, and the first-person 'he told me' in paragraph 4 establishes an authorial voice.
